'''Gorton:''' {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} {{legend0|#d72f30|70–80%}}
'''Sims:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Slade Gorton]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Slade Gorton]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsWA}} The '''1994 United States Senate election in Washington''' was held on November 8, 1994. Incumbent Senator [[Slade Gorton]] won re-election to a second consecutive term. As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, this was the last time a Republican, a man, or a non-Catholic won a U.S. Senate election in Washington. ==Background== Incumbent [[Slade Gorton]] was first [[1980 United States Senate election in Washington|elected]] U.S. senator from Washington in 1980. He narrowly lost his [[1986 United States Senate election in Washington|re-election bid]] in 1986. In 1988, he [[1988 United States Senate election in Washington|successfully ran]] for the state's other Senate seat. Leading up to the [[1994 United States Senate elections|1994 U.S. Senate elections]], Gorton was considered one of the most vulnerable [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbents. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] had swept the statewide elections in 1992—winning the [[1992 United States presidential election in Washington (state)|presidential]], [[1992 Washington gubernatorial election|gubernatorial]], and [[1992 United States Senate election in Washington|U.S. Senate]] races.{{cite news |last1=Lynch |first1=Jim |title=Gorton gets head start in 1994 Senate race |url=https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-27173954.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180930081329/https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-27173954.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=September 30, 2018 |url-access=subscription |access-date=September 30, 2018 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |via=[[HighBeam Research]] |location=Spokane, WA |date=February 24, 1994}} == Blanket primary == === Democratic === Many prominent Washington Democrats declined to contest the seat. Campaign analyst [[Charlie Cook]] of ''[[The Cook Political Report]]'' wrote that "the real top-notch folks just aren't running." [[Seattle]] mayor [[Norm Rice]] was encouraged by President [[Bill Clinton]] to run, but opted to stay in his position as mayor. The [[Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee]] unsuccessfully urged members of the state's U.S. House delegation to run. [[Ron Sims]], [[King County Council|King county councilman]], won the crowded Democratic primary with 17% of the vote. [[news presenter|News anchor]] Mike James came in second with 15%; all other candidates received less than 5%.{{cite news |title=Sims wins close race, zeros in on Gorton |url=https://products.kitsapsun.com/archive/1994/09-21/298675_senate__sims_wins_close_race__z.html |access-date=September 30, 2018 |work=[[Kitsap Sun]] |date=September 21, 1994 |language=en}} ====Candidates==== =====Declared===== * Scott Hardman, businessman * Mike James, news anchor * '''Nominee''': [[Ron Sims]], member of [[King County Council]] * Jesse Wineberry, member of the [[Washington House of Representatives]] =====Declined===== * [[Norm Dicks]], member of [[United States House of Representatives]] * [[Booth Gardner]], former [[governor of Washington]] * [[Norm Rice]], [[mayor of Seattle]] === Republican === Incumbent Gorton faced no serious competition for the Republican nomination. He won the primary with 52% of the vote. No other Republican candidate received any significant amount of support. ====Candidates==== * '''Nominee''': Slade Gorton, incumbent U.S. senator * Warren E. Hanson, [[commercial fishing|commercial fisherman]] * [[Mike the Mover]], [[perennial candidate]] === Results === [[File:1994 United States Senate primary election in Washington results map by county.svg|thumb|275px|Results by county {{collapsible list | title = {{legend|#e27f7f|Gorton}}|{{legend|#ffb2b2|40–50%}}|{{legend|#e27f7f|50–60%}}|{{legend|#d75d5d|60–70%}}|{{legend|#d72f30|70–80%}} }} ]] {{Election box begin no change |title = Blanket primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change |candidate = [[Slade Gorton]] (incumbent) |party = Republican Party (United States) |votes = 492,251 |percentage = 52.95% }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change |candidate = [[Ron Sims]] |party = Democratic Party (United States) |votes = 162,382 |percentage = 17.47% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |candidate = Mike James |party = Democratic Party (United States) |votes = 138,005 |percentage = 14.85% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |candidate = Scott Hardman |party = Democratic Party (United States) |votes = 29,973 |percentage = 3.32% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |candidate = Warren E. Hanson |party = Republican Party (United States) |votes = 26,628 |percentage = 2.86% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |candidate = Jesse Wineberry |party = Democratic Party (United States) |votes = 24,698 |percentage = 2.66% }} {{Election box total no change |votes = 873,937 |percentage = 100.00%}} {{Election box end}} == General election == === Candidates === * [[Slade Gorton]], incumbent U.S. senator (Republican) * [[Ron Sims]], member of King County Council (Democratic) === Campaign === Despite serving 12 years in the U.S. Senate, Gorton campaigned in 1994 as an outsider candidate.{{cite news |last1=Ammons |first1=David |title=Slade Gorton Grapples for Elusive Senate Seat |url=https://products.kitsapsun.com/archive/1994/06-05/296266_on_politics__slade_gorton_grapp.html |access-date=September 30, 2018 |work=[[Kitsap Sun]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=June 5, 1994 |language=en}}{{cite news |title=Landslide victory over Sims for Gorton |url=https://products.kitsapsun.com/archive/1994/11-09/301163_u_s__senate__landslide_victory_.html |access-date=September 30, 2018 |work=[[Kitsap Sun]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 9, 1994 |language=en}} He told crowds at [[campaign rally|campaign rallies]]: "If you want more of what you're getting from Washington, D.C., send one of my opponents. If you want a different direction, give a voice to balance by sending me back to the Senate."{{cite news |last1=Camden |first1=Jim |title=Gorton seeks image as tough pragmatist; Incumbent senator criticizes government |url=https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-27180421.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180930154446/https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-27180421.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=September 30, 2018 |url-access=subscription |access-date=September 30, 2018 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |via=HighBeam Research |location=Spokane, WA |date=September 16, 1994 }} He gained support among [[Agriculture|agricultural]], [[logging]], and [[mining]] groups in [[Eastern Washington]] for his criticism of federal regulations. Gorton called for opening up more federal forests to logging and changes to the [[Endangered Species Act of 1973|Endangered Species Act]]. Sims campaigned in support of the [[Presidency of Bill Clinton|Clinton administration]]. He accused Gorton of obstructing President Clinton's [[Clinton health care plan of 1993|healthcare]] and crime reforms. The Sims campaign also attempted to portray Gorton as out of touch with the average Washingtonian. Sims was the first [[African American]] U.S. Senate candidate in state history to advance to the general election, although the issue of [[Race (human categorization)|race]] was rarely addressed during the campaign. === Results === {{Election box begin | title=1994 United States Senate election in Washington{{Cite news|url=https://www.sos.wa.gov/elections/results_report.aspx?e=15&c=&c2=&t=985&t2=&p=&p2=&y=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241208192240/https://www.sos.wa.gov/elections/results_report.aspx?e=15&c=&c2=&t=985&t2=&p=&p2=&y=|archive-date=2024-12-08|url-status=dead|title=Elections Search Results November 1994 General U.
